Key cross-cutting observations: (1) The credential-missing badge in workspace-detail.js is the most significant UX gap — it is lost on page reload because the state is in-memory only. This should seed WP-001 of the next cycle. (2) All 5 security audits found 0 Critical/High issues; the 4 Medium items (host-coherence guard, hostname leak in error messages, missing audit logging, unvalidated host format) are coherent and should be addressed together in a dedicated security-hardening WP. (3) WP-007 was partially pre-implemented when claimed — the Developer fixed orchestrator compile errors during WP-006 execution and the WP-007 pipeline only added the missing ErrorLogManager integration tests. The ledger correctly reflects COMPLETE status for both WPs. (4) The overall architecture of the multi-credential system (GitCredentialEntry[], resolveCredential(), injectCredentialToken()) is clean, well-tested, and extensible. The OWASP A01 caller-contract for host coherence is the one design obligation that future call-site authors must be made aware of.

outcome_summary: The project successfully migrated the repo-parallelizer credential system from a single-token-per-host model (Record<string,string>) to a named multi-credential array model (GitCredentialEntry[]) across the full vertical stack — core types, config parsing with backward-compatible auto-migration, REST API, orchestrators, and the GUI. All 10 work packages were delivered with 896/896 server tests and 199/199 GUI tests passing at zero TypeScript compile errors, and 5 security audits found no Critical or High severity issues. The primary open items for the next cycle are: removing the now-dead legacy injectCredentials() function, persisting credential-error badge state across page reloads in the workspace detail view, and addressing the four documented Medium security observations in a dedicated hardening work package.
